# Siteaccesses and languages of sevenx_multisite

This page is for administrators and hosts who run a `sevenx_multisite` installation and need to know which
siteaccesses it has, what is set in each, and what happens with the languages chosen in the setup. Everything here is
read from `settings/sevenx-multi-site-installer.php` and the kernel step `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php`.

## Contents

1. [The siteaccesses at a glance](#the-siteaccesses-at-a-glance)
2. [The user siteaccess](#the-user-siteaccess)
3. [Bold Agency: bold and bold_ger](#bold-agency-bold-and-bold_ger)
4. [admin, editor and adminui](#admin-editor-and-adminui)
5. [Settings shared by all siteaccesses](#settings-shared-by-all-siteaccesses)
6. [Languages and translation siteaccesses](#languages-and-translation-siteaccesses)

## The siteaccesses at a glance

| Siteaccess | Made by | Serves | Design |
|---|---|---|---|
| `site` (the setup's user siteaccess) | `CreateSites`, then the installer | Fit & Healthy | `media` |
| one per extra language (for example `ger`) | `createTranslationSiteAccesses()` | Fit & Healthy in that language | copied from `site` |
| `bold` | `createSecondarySiteaccesses()` with settings shipped by `sevenx_themes_media` | Bold Agency in English | `media` |
| `bold_ger` | the same | Bold Agency in German | `media` |
| `admin` (the setup's admin siteaccess) | `CreateSites`, then the installer | the administration | `admin4l` |
| `editor` | the kernel's `createEditorSiteAccess()` after the post-install | content editing | `editor` |
| `adminui` | `postInstallCreateAdminUISiteaccess()` (or the kernel) when `exp_adminui` is installed | the administration in the Admin UI design | from `exp_adminui` |

`bold` and `bold_ger` are added only when their settings exist, either already in `settings/siteaccess/<name>/` or
shipped by an extension in `extension/*/settings/siteaccess/<name>/` (`secondarySiteaccessIsAvailable()`). The theme
extension `sevenx_themes_media` ships both.

## The user siteaccess

`postInstallUserSiteaccessINIUpdate()` and `siteINISettings()` write to `settings/siteaccess/site/`:

| File and group | Settings |
|---|---|
| `site.ini [DesignSettings]` | `SiteDesign=media`, `AdditionalSiteDesignList` `ezwebin`, `standard`, `base` |
| `site.ini [SiteSettings]` | `SiteName` (the site title), `SiteDescription` "An Exponential multisite installation", `IndexPage` and `DefaultPage` `/content/view/full/<home node>`, `RootNodeDepth`, `SiteURL`, `MetaDataArray`, `LoginPage=embedded`, `AdditionalLoginFormActionURL` pointing at the admin's `/user/login` |
| `site.ini [SiteAccessSettings]` | `RequireUserLogin=false`, `ShowHiddenNodes=false`, `ForceVirtualHost=true`, `PathPrefix`, `RelatedSiteAccessList` |
| `site.ini [RegionalSettings]` | `Locale` and `ContentObjectLocale` (the primary language, else `eng-US`), `SiteLanguageList`, `ShowUntranslatedObjects=disabled` |
| `site.ini [Session]` | `SessionNamePerSiteAccess=disabled` |
| `site.ini [FileSettings]` | `VarDir=var/site` |
| `content.ini [NodeSettings]` | `RootNode` = the home node |

The home node is found by its remote id `media-n-939` with plain SQL (`homeNodeID()`), because node ids differ between
installations and language-filtered lookups return nothing while the install runs. `PathPrefix` is the URL alias form
of the home node's name ("Fit & Healthy"), written by `postInstallSetSiteHomeAndPrefix()`, so the site's pages are
served without the home node's own path segment. `RequireUserLogin=false` is written explicitly because "the shipped
settings/site.ini sets RequireUserLogin=true".

## Bold Agency: bold and bold_ger

Bold Agency is a second site in the same installation, below the home node `media-n-940`. Its siteaccesses are
reached by path on the main site's address (`/bold/`, `/bold_ger/`); they have no host or port of their own.

`sevenx_themes_media` ships `settings/siteaccess/bold` and `bold_ger` with the design `media`, `SiteName=Bold Agency`,
the languages (`bold`: `eng-US`; `bold_ger`: `ger-DE` then `eng-US`, `TranslationList=ger-DE`) and a switcher map
`TranslationSA[bold]=English`, `TranslationSA[bold_ger]=Deutsch`. The installer then writes
`settings/siteaccess/bold*/site.ini.append.php` itself (`createSecondarySiteaccesses()`):

- no `[DatabaseSettings]`, on purpose: "the database is declared once in settings/override and inherited";
- `RequireUserLogin=false`, `ShowHiddenNodes=false`, `RelatedSiteAccessList`, `PathPrefix` from the home node's name;
- `SiteDesign=media` with `simple`, `ezwebin`, `standard`, `base` after it;
- `IndexPage`, `DefaultPage`, `SiteURL` (the user siteaccess's address followed by `/bold` or `/bold_ger`),
  `LoginPage=embedded` and the admin login form address.

`IndexPage` and `PathPrefix` cannot be left to the theme. As the installer's comment explains, `settings/siteaccess`
outranks `extension/<ext>/settings/siteaccess`, "and the extension can only ship node ids from whichever installation
it was exported on".

## admin, editor and adminui

`adminINISettings()` and `postInstallAdminSiteaccessINIUpdate()` write to `settings/siteaccess/admin/`:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| `SiteDesign` | `admin4l`, with `admin4`, `admin3`, `admin2`, `admin` in `AdditionalSiteDesignList` |
| `RequireUserLogin`, `ShowHiddenNodes`, `ForceVirtualHost` | `true` |
| `LoginPage` | `custom` |
| `SiteName` | Admin |
| `RegionalSettings` | the primary language, `SiteLanguageList`, and `TranslationSA` (the user siteaccess and its translations) |
| `ExtensionSettings ActiveAccessExtensions` | `expai` and `exp_adminui`, each only when the extension is installed |
| `content.ini RootNode` | the parent of the home node |
| other files | `toolbar.ini`, `menu.ini` (header tabs), `contentstructuremenu.ini`, `override.ini`, `icon.ini` (`crystal-admin`), `viewcache.ini`, `ezoe.ini`, `odf.ini` |

The editor siteaccess is made by the kernel after the post-install: `createEditorSiteAccess()` copies every
`*.ini.append.php` of the admin siteaccess and sets `SiteDesign=editor`, `AdditionalSiteDesignList` `admin4l`,
`admin4`, `admin3`, `admin2`, `admin`, `ExtensionSettingsSiteAccess=admin` and `SiteName=Editor`. The `adminui`
siteaccess is made from the admin siteaccess's files with the Admin UI design chain; it "is reached by URI only
(/adminui)". See [Setup wizard and the editor siteaccess](../../../features/6.0/setup-wizard-and-editor-siteaccess.md) and
[Admin UI](../../../features/6.0/exp-adminui.md).

## Settings shared by all siteaccesses

`commonSiteINISettings()` writes `settings/override/site.ini.append.php`, which every siteaccess inherits:

| Group | Settings |
|---|---|
| `[SiteAccessSettings]` | `AvailableSiteAccessList` and `RelatedSiteAccessList` (every served siteaccess), `MatchOrder` `uri;host` (`uri;port` with port access), `PathPrefixExclude` `Media` and `Users`, `ForceVirtualHost=true`, and `HostMatchMapItems` with host access |
| `[PortAccessSettings]` | one entry per siteaccess with port access |
| `[SiteSettings]` | `SiteList`, `DefaultAccess` (the user siteaccess), `RootNodeDepth=1` |
| `[ExtensionSettings]` | `ActiveExtensions` |
| `[DatabaseSettings]` | the driver and connection the install ran on |
| `[Session]` | `SessionNameHandler=custom`, so the admin keeps a session of its own |
| `[UserSettings]` | `LogoutRedirect=/`, plus the 2FA login handler when installed |

`MatchOrder` starts with `uri` because the Bold siteaccesses are reached by path. No `[RegionalSettings]` is written
to `settings/override`: it outranks every siteaccess, and a language set there "pinned the German Bold siteaccess to
eng-US".

## Languages and translation siteaccesses

The first language chosen in the setup is the primary language and is served by the user siteaccess. For every other
chosen language `createTranslationSiteAccesses()` copies the user siteaccess into a new one:

1. The name comes from `languageNameFromLocale()` in `kernel/classes/ezsiteinstaller.php`: the part before the dash
   (`ger-DE` becomes `ger`). When two chosen languages share that part, the later one gets its country (`eng_gb`).
2. When the user siteaccess is `bold`, the name gets the prefix `bold_`.
3. A name that is already taken (`site`, `admin`, `editor`, `adminui`, `bold`, `bold_ger`, the user and admin
   siteaccesses) gets the country, then a number.
4. The copy gets `Locale` and `ContentObjectLocale` of its language, `TextTranslation=enabled` (disabled for
   `eng-GB`), a `SiteLanguageList` with its language first, the site title and home page of the user siteaccess, and
   `ExtensionSettingsSiteAccess` set to the user siteaccess so it uses the same theme settings.
5. `postInstallSetSiteHomeAndPrefix()` gives it the same `PathPrefix` and copies the user siteaccess's
   `menu.ini.append.php` to it.

The bundled content is in `eng-US`. When `eng-US` is not among the chosen languages it is added after them as a
fallback in every `SiteLanguageList` (`fallback_locales`), so pages still show their content.

> **Note**
> With port access, the translation siteaccesses count up from the user siteaccess's port, leaving out the admin and
> editor ports. With host access they use the site's host name.
